subject: Re: Token throughput & SLA deep-dive — scheduling
messages:
From: Phil Morrison <phil@edgescale.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Token throughput targets + architecture deep-dive request

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the chat last week — EdgeScale is excited to validate Redwood for our inference layer. We're putting together a short architecture-level deep-dive focused on sustained token throughput, burst behaviour, and the SLA envelope (latency P95/P99 targets).

High-level asks from our side:
- Confirm whether Redwood can support sustained 120k tokens/sec for our 8-request concurrent profile (average 1.5k tokens per request) with 95th %ile tail latency under ~150ms for streaming responses.
- Discuss KV cache warmup strategies and prefix cache reuse for repeated user sessions.
- Walk through fallback routing & quantized variant tradeoffs for cost reductions.

I've attached our load profile + a short list of customer questions (edgescale_load_profile.csv, customer_qs.pdf). Can we schedule a 60–75 minute session next week to include: you (architecture lead), service runtime, and product to align on expectations? Prefer windows (PDT): Tue 2026-05-12 09:00–11:00 or Wed 2026-05-13 13:00–15:00.

Thanks — happy to be flexible.

Phil Morrison
Head of ML Engineering | EdgeScale
phil@edgescale.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

- Tuesday 2026-05-12 10:00–11:15 (dry-run 09:30–09:45)
- Wednesday 2026-05-13 14:00–15:15 (dry-run 13:30–13:45)

Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 07:42:00 -0700

Irene — appreciate the quick reply. Wed 2026-05-13 14:00–15:15 PDT works well for our team; please send a calendar invite.

A couple of clarifications for the agenda so we can prep:
- Prioritize a short slot for "prefix-caching and KV warmup" (15–20 mins) — it's the biggest open risk to our SLA.
- Expected targets: sustained 120k tokens/sec across 8 concurrent request streams (avg 1.5k tokens each), with bursts up to 200k tokens/sec for short windows. Our latency goal is P95 <= 150ms for streaming first-byte for these profiles; P99 ideally < 350ms.
- We're keen to understand how quantized variants affect tail latency under this workload (e.g., int8 vs fp16).

We'd like Redwood to run a short 15-minute synthetic run ahead of the meeting using the CSV so we can verify warmup characteristics. Can you reserve a slot and give us an example runbook for the dry-run?

I'll attach the CSV and our internal questions again in case they didn't come through earlier.

—Phil
